# biocroxytest <a href="https://xec-cm.github.io/biocroxytest/"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="biocroxytest website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/workflows/R-CMD-check-bioc/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/actions)
[![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg?style=flat-square)](https://makeapullrequest.com)
[![GitHub issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/xec-cm/biocroxytest)](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/issues)
[![GitHub pulls](https://img.shields.io/github/issues-pr/xec-cm/biocroxytest)](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/pulls)
<!-- badges: end -->

Write ordinary and Bioconductor long tests alongside the code they cover.
`biocroxytest` turns `@tests` and `@longtests` tags into standard testthat files.
The approach builds on `r BiocStyle::Githubpkg("mikldk/roxytest")` and
`r BiocStyle::Githubpkg("r-lib/roxygen2")`.

## Installation instructions

Get the latest stable `R` release from [CRAN](http://cran.r-project.org/). Then 
install `biocroxytest` from [Bioconductor](http://bioconductor.org/) using the 
following code:

```{r 'install', eval = FALSE}
# Not yet on Bioconductor
# if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
#     install.packages("BiocManager")
# }
# 
# BiocManager::install("biocroxytest")
```

And the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest)
with:

```{r 'install_dev', eval = FALSE}
BiocManager::install("xec-cm/biocroxytest")
```

## Example

Set up ordinary tests with `usethis::use_testthat()` and long tests with
`biocroxytest::use_longtests()`. Run the setup for the suites you use and list
`testthat` in Suggests. Add the generator to your existing roxygen configuration
in DESCRIPTION.

```
Roxygen: list(roclets = c("namespace", "rd", "biocroxytest::tests_roclet"))
```

Write the body of each test in a tag. For example, in `R/functions.R`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#' A function to do x
#' 
#' @param x A number
#' 
#' @tests
#' expect_equal(foo(0), 0)
#'
#' @longtests 
#' expect_equal(foo(2), sqrt(2))
#' expect_error(foo("a string"))
#' 
#' @return something
foo <- function(x) {
  return(sqrt(x))
}

#' A function to do y
#' 
#' @param x Character vector
#' @param y Character vector
#' 
#' @longtests 
#' expect_equal(bar("A", "B"), paste("A", "B", sep = "/"))
#' 
#' @export
bar <- function(x, y) {
  paste0(x, "/", y)
}
```

Run `roxygen2::roxygenise()`. The ordinary tests go to
`tests/testthat/test-roxytest-tests-functions.R` and the long tests go to
`longtests/testthat/test-biocroxytest-longtests-functions.R`. Each suite
uses its own testthat runner and helpers. The package only needs testthat to run
the generated tests.

For a long-test-only configuration, continue using
`biocroxytest::longtests_roclet`.

## Migrate from roxytest

Preview the migration in a clean branch or disposable copy. Replace
`roxytest::testthat_roclet` and, if present, `biocroxytest::longtests_roclet`
with `biocroxytest::tests_roclet`. Regenerate and inspect the diff, then run
your test suites. The generator retains the `test-roxytest-tests-` and
`test-roxytest-testexamples-` prefixes and updates the ownership header.
Use the default `clean = FALSE` with custom roclets. The unified roclet
cleans up obsolete generated tests after validating both suites on every run.

For shared `@rdname` topics, each tag follows its own source file. If roxytest
previously merged those blocks, a test can move or change description. Review
and migrate any affected snapshots before adopting the generated files.
To revert a migration, restore both the previous configuration and its
generated files.

## Test documented examples

Add `@testexamples` with the assertions to run after the examples on the
same topic. Each tag produces an ordinary test with its own example variables.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#' Increment an integer
#' @examples
#' value <- increment(2L)
#' @testexamples
#' expect_identical(value, 3L)
increment <- function(x) x + 1L
```

The roclet runs `@examples` and `@example` in roxygen's block order, including
direct examples from blocks that contribute to the same Rd topic. R's Rd rules omit
`\dontrun{}` and execute `\dontshow{}` and `\donttest{}`. Use `@examplesIf`
for examples that depend on an optional resource. Its condition is evaluated
during the test, after the preceding examples. If it is false, testthat skips
that test and its assertions. Rd platform directives are resolved on the
machine generating the tests. This workflow uses direct examples. It excludes
inherited examples and templates, and rejects Rd `\Sexpr{}` expressions.

## Share a test across named cases

With `biocroxytest::tests_roclet`, put a literal list in an `@testCases`
tag. Each case chooses a suite and can prepare its own inputs. The shared
body runs once per case.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#' @testCases arithmetic
#' list(
#'   cases = list(
#'     small = list(suite = "tests", setup = { x <- 2L }),
#'     large = list(suite = "longtests", setup = { x <- 1000L })
#'   ),
#'   test = { expect_identical(increment(x), x + 1L) }
#' )
increment <- function(x) x + 1L
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
before <- biocroxytest::test_case_plan()
roxygen2::roxygenise()
biocroxytest::run_test_case("arithmetic/large")

# After editing the declarations:
biocroxytest::compare_test_plans(before, biocroxytest::test_case_plan())
```

IDs use the group and case names and survive changes of file or suite.
The planner reads declarations without loading the consumer package.
The generator leaves fixture creation to test execution. The local runner
uses the selected suite's testthat helpers, setup and teardown in a temporary
copy to protect existing snapshots. Run the full suite to review snapshot
changes and exercise any custom suite runner.

## Record named test results

```{r, eval=FALSE}
evidence <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan()
evidence$cases
```

The report records each case's status and duration alongside the revision
fingerprint and R environment. Pass `ids` to record selected cases.
`completed` requires a passing assertion and reaching the end of the case
without skips. Failed assertions, explicit skips, incomplete execution
and missing results have their own statuses. A stale generated case is
incomplete. Regenerate tests before recording evidence.

Each case runs in a fresh R session and a temporary copy, with its suite's
testthat helpers, setup and teardown.

## Replay a failed case

```{r, eval=FALSE}
evidence <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(ids = "alignment/hdf5", seed = 42L)
record <- biocroxytest::write_test_replay(evidence, "alignment/hdf5", "../alignment-failure.rds")
record$command
replayed <- biocroxytest::replay_test_case("../alignment-failure.rds")
replayed$comparison
```

Export a case whose status is `failed` and keep the RDS file outside the
package source. Replay uses the recorded R seed and checks the package
revision and fixture identity before running. It compares the failure
messages and available source locations and reports environment changes. Keep the
matching source and fixture inputs available.

## Pin test fixtures

Add `fs` to your package's Suggests and a `fixtures` list to the named case.
For example, put `fixture.tsv` in the case's `tests/testthat` directory and compute its
checksum with `tools::md5sum("tests/testthat/fixture.tsv")`.

```r
#' @testCases table
#' list(
#'   cases = list(
#'     small = list(suite = "tests", fixtures = list(
#'       data = list(source = "fixture.tsv", md5 = "<32-digit checksum>")
#'     ))
#'   ),
#'   test = { expect_gt(nrow(read.delim(fixture_paths[["data"]])), 0L) }
#' )
```

For an HTTPS source, install BiocFileCache and run
`run_test_plan(download_fixtures = TRUE)` to populate the cache.
Later runs can use the cache offline. The report's
`fixtures` field records each check. A missing or changed required fixture
blocks the case. With `required = FALSE`, the case can handle an unavailable
fixture through an `NA` path. Standard testthat runs verify local files and
skip cases that require a remote fixture.

## Reduce a paired failure

Use `reduce_paired_failure()` to find a smaller SummarizedExperiment for
an ordinary regression test. The pilot supports two conditions, one sample
per condition and pair, and an additive design with the pair and condition
as main effects.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
reduced <- biocroxytest::reduce_paired_failure(
  x, pair = "subject", condition = "visit", design = ~ subject + visit,
  check = check_known_failure
)
dim(reduced$data)
reduced$failure
```

Implement `check_known_failure()` to run the failing operation and return
a stable identifier for the specific failure, or `NULL` if it is absent.
The reducer checks the original data, tries smaller subsets of features
and complete pairs, and checks the final subset again. It preserves a
full-rank design with residual degrees of freedom. Review the subset and
use it in an ordinary test of the expected correct behavior.

## Check generated tests in CI

List the generated files, their source files, and their suites with
`biocroxytest::generated_test_inventory()`. To check that those files
match the source, run this after installing the package's development
dependencies:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla -e 'biocroxytest::check_generated_tests()'
```

Run the command from the consumer package root, or pass its path to the
function. The check uses the configured biocroxytest roclet in a temporary
copy. It exits with an error if generated files are missing, changed, or
obsolete. Regenerate with `roxygen2::roxygenise()` and commit the resulting
changes. Manual tests and snapshots are excluded from the comparison.
